extracted.intended_audience: UK patent examiners, patent attorneys, applicants, and other practitioners interacting with UKIPO practice
extracted.subtask_description: Official Manual of Patent Practice (MoPP) guidance used by UKIPO examiners and practitioners to interpret the Patents Act 1977 and related practice when assessing patent applications in the UK, including patentability, exclusions, sufficiency, form/content, search, examination and term issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Section 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall be granted only if: 1. Invention is new; 2. Involves an inventive step; 3. Capable of industrial application; 4. Not excluded subject matter (Section 1(2)-(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching statutory threshold used throughout the MoPP; the Manual follows the Patents Act 1977 section by section and annotates how each limb is applied in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Section 2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is treated as a standalone statutory requirement (Section 2) and is examined in light of prior art and disclosures; see MoPP commentary on how search and prior art affect novelty assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Section 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must involve an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive step is a substantive requirement (Section 3); MoPP guidance aligns with established approaches to identifying the person skilled in the art, the closest prior art, the distinguishing features and whether those features would have been obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (Section 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be capable of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4 requires that the claimed subject-matter can be made or used in any kind of industry; MoPP explains how to determine practicality and real-world applicability during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter (Section 1(2) — 'as such')
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded items: discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods; aesthetic creations; schemes, rules, methods for performing mental acts, playing games, doing business; programs for computers; presentation of information (all 'as such').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors EPC Article 52 exclusions. The MoPP explains that these categories are not patentable 'as such' and provides context for when subject-matter that involves or uses these things nevertheless makes a patentable technical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aerotel/Macrossan four-step test (software/business methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: UK courts apply a four-step test: 1. Properly construe the claim; 2. Identify the actual contribution; 3. Ask whether it falls solely within the excluded subject matter; 4. Check whether the actual contribution is technical in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This test is the UK-specific approach used by courts (and reflected in examination practice) to determine whether computer-implemented or business-method claims are excluded. MoPP uses the test to frame claim construction and contribution analysis for such inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-implemented inventions — technical contribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical contribution required (not just executable nature of computer programs); distinguish between technical contributions and business/non-technical results; aligned with EPO practice but with UK-specific test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MoPP provides targeted guidance on examining computer-implemented inventions: examiners must identify a technical contribution beyond mere software execution or non-technical business effects. The Manual clarifies examples, contrasts with business/non-technical outcomes, and notes alignment with EPO approaches while applying the Aerotel/Macrossan framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency / description (Section 14(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must disclose the invention clearly enough and completely enough for it to be performed by a person skilled in the art and must cover the entire scope of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 14(3) insufficiency is a ground for refusal; MoPP explains requirements for enabling disclosure, scope coverage (no gaps between claim breadth and supporting description), and what constitutes adequate guidance for a skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of the application (Section 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements as to the form and content of the patent application as set out in Section 14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MoPP comments on formal requirements, necessary parts of the specification, claims and drawings, and procedural expectations; Section 14 has been subject to recent substantive updates (noted Jan 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search (Section 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search procedures and expectations under Section 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MoPP describes how prior-art searches are conducted, what is searched, how search reports are prepared and used in later examination and prosecution decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedures (Section 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination rules and practice under Section 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MoPP gives detailed examiner guidance on examination steps, applying patentability criteria, handling objections, and interacting with applicants during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for placing application in order (Section 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and timelines for putting an application in order under Section 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual explains statutory and procedural time limits for responding to examination and objections; Section 20 was among the sections with substantive changes in the Jan 2026 update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term, lapse and restoration (Sections 25–37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions relating to patent term, lapse, and restoration found in Sections 25–37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MoPP details how term calculations, lapsing for non-payment or failure to act, and restoration processes are handled by UKIPO (procedural requirements, timelines and evidentiary standards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPCs) for medicinal and plant protection products
rubrics_metrics.description: SPC rules and practice for extending protection of medicinal and plant protection products (recent substantive updates noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Jan 2026 update included substantive changes relating to SPCs; MoPP provides guidance on eligibility, filing and interaction between SPCs and patent term/rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic/practical differences from US practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Key strategic differences: more restrictive software/business-method eligibility; focus on 'technical contribution'; no best mode requirement; no information disclosure statement/duty of candour; generally cheaper filing and examination fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section in the MoPP summary explains how applicants and practitioners should adjust prosecution strategy when moving between UK and US practice (e.g., draft claims to emphasise technical contribution for software, do not rely on best mode disclosure, adapt prior-art disclosure practices to UK norms).
